title: Rust engine parity sweep: two audits against the JavaScript game
summary: Two audits compared the Rust engine with the frozen JavaScript game. Nine pull requests (#289 to #297) fixed what they found, covering menus, links, controllers, multiplayer, desktop loading and settings, page transitions, WebGL context restore and the desktop soundtrack. Eight are merged; #297, the second runtime pass, is queued to merge.
details: Arcade flips (#289): the ride switched flips off whenever Arcade was on, so the flip controller was rebuilt every step and the bike barely rotated (about 0.23 rad/s instead of about 6.5). Fixed for every input. Touch now also feeds the 360 axis and the flip requests from the flip zones, swipes and the two-finger pad. Peak commanded rates on the env01 ramp now match the JavaScript game: touch backflip 6.53 vs 6.65 rad/s, touch 360 7.25 vs 7.25, keyboard 6.42 vs 6.42.

Runtime and multiplayer (#290): Alpha air slow-mo stays off in rooms. Reserved FREERD codes cannot be hosted, and a FREERD invite or ?room= link opens Free Ride instead of failing with a 400. Contact shadows now use a measured rest lift in normal play. Remote rider models are evicted past 20 cached. Rider contacts are sampled per step. The race-over music hold shortens its fade when little song remains. Remote engine voices are ranked by distance to the player's vehicle. The relay inbox drops pose floods and closes on a control-message backlog.

Menus, links, controllers (#291): Restart Race in the pause menu reloads the whole event, Clear binding clears the highlighted row, Left/Right and Start behave as in the JavaScript menus, and a blur cancels a binding capture. Main-menu Settings share the rides' device defaults. A bad ride link explains itself, and a bare ?room= link joins through Join Lobby. Garage previews show loading and unavailable states. Race results always offer Quit Event. Rumble goes to the pad in use, Auto ignores resting axes, and pads with more than 17 buttons or 4 axes are read. Desktop gets system clipboard copy and paste for ride and invite links.

Desktop platform (#292): loads and room joins no longer block the event loop (ENV01 loads of 2.25 to 2.94 s now take at most 279 to 359 ms per event-loop turn). Metal and DX12 cap the render scale at 1.5 backing pixels per logical pixel with the browser's step-down, and desktop Auto graphics comes from the GPU adapter. The settings file merges writes so a stale copy cannot drop the multiplayer session key. The display is kept awake while riding. Jukebox seek works on desktop. A lost GPU device is recorded and recovered by reopening the ride from its start, instead of panicking.

Page transitions (#293): every menu page slides in from 36 px over 240 ms on the JavaScript game's curve, in the frontend, Settings/Jukebox and every pause page, with reduced motion opening pages at rest.

Idle host (#294): a guest joining a host sitting still on the start line could spawn on top of it. A rider alone in a room now sends a presence pose at most once a second (every 5 s while paused), and an arrival waits up to 15 s for a pose before its usual meet tries. The stopped-host scenario now meets at 10 ft instead of leaving met null with the guest about 7 ft away.

WebGL context restore (#295): after a lost and restored context the web build rebuilds the scene, rider and CPU models, wheel effects, HUD and menus in place instead of reloading the ride link, so a single-player ride keeps its position, step count, race state and room slot. While the context is lost the engine draws nothing, takes no input, suspends sound, keeps the room connected and shows Restoring graphics.

Desktop soundtrack (#296): the desktop apps play the same 21 remastered AAC songs as the web, bundled in the content pack so they work offline. Playback is decoded in Rust with the encoder priming removed so start, seek and length match the browser, with sample-accurate seeks. A missing or damaged song falls back to the original VAG. The content pack grows from 454.4 MB to 541.9 MB, so each archive grows by an estimated 87 MB.

Second runtime pass (#297, queued to merge): other riders are drawn at any distance, remote engines are heard from the drawn camera, the speed-rush mask is written only by the player's vehicle, a live room's ride keeps simulating behind Change ATV and Select Track, vegetation stale-fade reset follows a per-frame serial, race countdown and autopilot steps turn off flips and realistic train, and ambient effects share the fog-based far distance.

Discoveries: the JavaScript menu exit slide is a snapshot of the menu canvas, which HD screens and pause panels clear on every layout. The snapshot had 0 opaque pixels on title, main and multiplayer, so it fades an empty canvas and the Rust engine draws no exit. Idle-host guests never met because a rider alone in a room sent no poses, so the relay had nothing to hand an arriving guest. The shadow rest lift was only measured under autodrive, so normal play drew with the 1.5 ft default. The 'CPU quad missing' path is unreachable, since every original course ships its group file and the loader refuses a short roster.

Verification: host-only focused Rust and browser checks listed in each PR body. Rust fmt, clippy with warnings denied, unit tests and wasm builds ran on the touched crates. Content browser tests included menu_parity, menu_transitions, context_loss, links, pause, race, hud, settings, jukebox and alpha, plus the new arcade-touch test. Local-relay multiplayer tests covered room_front, audio, tags, presence, pause, menu, dropin, train and freeride, plus new idle-host and context tests. Desktop checks on an Apple M4 included a native 60 fps ride, a simulated device loss, the real remaster pack through an ignored acceptance test, and verification of 21 of 21 songs. CI ran on each PR.
limitation: All measurements are host-only (headless Chromium and an Apple M4 Mac); nothing was verified on a physical phone. Windows and Linux desktop playback and render scale were not run, and no desktop release was built or published. play.html has not been switched to the Rust engine; the user decides when. A menus-and-flows batch is still in progress. #297 has no browser test with a rider beyond 864 ft and its speed-rush and vegetation changes were not compared visually. After a web context restore Chromium logs about 20 console warnings, and the notice is the status strip rather than the JavaScript loading panel.
